title: The Ridge Where Altitude Becomes Addition

features.name: altitude marker
features.desc-on-touch: A brass theodolite fixed to a stone cairn, its numbers etched by three generations of surveyors. The readings were never the same twice.

features.name: vista pool
features.desc-on-touch: A dew-pool at the ridge's edge, holding the light like a small sky. The valley reflects upside-down through it—closer than it ought to be.

features.name: counting glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A plaque of tally marks spiralling inward toward a center. When you count forward you reach the end; when you count backward, you're still going.

features.name: shelter hut
features.desc-on-touch: A small stone shelter built to weather. Inside, a logbook thick with pencilled notes: each entry swears the ridge is a different height today than yesterday.

features.name: stepping descent
features.desc-on-touch: A cascade of flat rocks leading downslope, each one counted and numbered in fading paint. The count skips—74, 75, 77—as if some steps have learned to hide.

inscription: the height teaches counting, and counting teaches the height back

file.name: Ridge_Measurement_Logs_1970s_Disputed.txt
file.note: Altitude records taken from the same ridge across decades—each set contradicts the last, as if the ridge has learned to rise and sink with whoever reads it

reverie.title: REVERIE — dusk at the high ridge
narr: You stand here with her, the theodolite steady on its tripod.
The valley below holds the day like wine it hasn't drunk yet.
Her pencil marks the reading: 847.2. Yesterday's was 846.1.
She meets your eye. The ridge itself is drifting, she says.
You both know better. But the light won't let you argue.
The numbers will argue themselves once you've left.
